html:
The Bunurong, also spelt Boonwurrung, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Kulin alliance, the traditional owners of the coast of Victoria from the Werribee River around Port Phillip and Western Port to Wilsons Promontory. Their country includes part of today's Melbourne.

They lived from the bays, the swamps and the coastal heath, and shared law and marriage ties with the other Kulin nations, above all the Wurundjeri of the Yarra valley. To the east lay the Gunai Kurnai, with whom there was old enmity.

In the early 1800s sealers on Bass Strait raided the coast and carried off women. Settlers from Van Diemen's Land founded Melbourne in 1835, and the Bunurong leader Derrimut warned them of a planned attack that year. Within twenty years disease, the loss of land and violence had cut their numbers to a small remnant. Their descendants are recognised today as the traditional owners of the area.
